title: Authentication failures fail open
description: require_auth catches the 401 HTTPException raised when no valid user exists, logs it, sets g.user to None, and still invokes the protected handler. Any protected endpoint that does not immediately dereference g.user can therefore be used anonymously.
evidence: GET /orders/1 without an Authorization header returned HTTP 200 and the complete order. The exception handler at lines 55-58 catches all exceptions and calls f(*args, **kwargs) after the failed check.

title: Trailing-slash admin route bypasses staff authorization
description: The global admin check compares request.path against exact registered route strings. The refunds route accepts both slash forms via strict_slashes=False, but the alternate form is not in admin_paths, allowing an unauthenticated caller to execute the staff-only refund handler.
evidence: POST /admin/refunds/ with no Authorization header and {"order_id":1,"amount_pence":1} returned HTTP 200 and created a refund. The route is declared at shopapi/admin.py:52 with strict_slashes=False, while the check uses exact request.path membership at lines 36-41.

title: Order lookup does not enforce ownership
description: show_order calls get_order rather than own_order and never compares customer_id with the authenticated user. Any caller who knows an order ID can read another customer's order details, including totals, payment amount, items, and refunds.
evidence: GET /orders/1 without authentication returned HTTP 200 with the order contents because authentication also fails open. Even after fixing that decorator, the handler at lines 46-49 still invokes get_order directly instead of the ownership-checking own_order helper.

title: Token refresh accepts unsigned attacker-controlled JWTs
description: The refresh endpoint disables JWT signature verification and uses only the attacker-supplied sub claim to load a user. An attacker can name any existing account and obtain a newly signed access token for it.
evidence: POST /auth/refresh with an unsigned JWT containing {"sub":1} returned HTTP 200 and a fresh signed token. Lines 101-105 decode with verify_signature=False and do not require proof of possession of a valid refresh token.

title: Unauthenticated basket cookie is deserialized with pickle
description: The basket cookie is client-controlled and has no integrity protection, but read_basket base64-decodes it and passes it to pickle.loads. A crafted cookie can execute arbitrary Python code when any endpoint reads the basket, including the public basket endpoint.
evidence: read_basket at lines 15-23 calls pickle.loads on request.cookies['basket']; GET /basket at lines 44-46 invokes it without authentication or a signature check.

title: Product search is vulnerable to SQL injection
description: The search term is concatenated into a SQL statement rather than passed as a bound parameter, allowing query predicates to be altered by a requester.
evidence: The query at lines 40-42 interpolates q into both LIKE clauses. GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201%3D1-- returned all six products instead of a literal search result.

title: Staff review report is vulnerable to stored SQL injection
description: The review report interpolates a customer's display_name into a SQL string. display_name is user-editable through /account, so a customer can store SQL syntax that is executed when staff request the report.
evidence: Lines 77-81 construct the query with f"... WHERE r.author_name = '{customer['display_name']}' ...". update_account at shopapi/auth.py:116-125 writes the untrusted display_name.

title: Review bodies are rendered as trusted HTML
description: Review text is stored without sanitization and rendered with Jinja's safe filter. A user can submit HTML or script content that executes for visitors viewing the product page.
evidence: add_review stores body directly at shopapi/products.py:82-91, and product.html renders r.body using {{ r.body|safe }} at line 13.

title: Payment status timeout marks orders as paid
description: A timeout contacting the payment provider is treated as a successful payment. The order is then moved to processing and paid_pence is set to total_pence, allowing fulfillment during provider outages or induced timeouts.
evidence: confirm_payment catches requests.Timeout at lines 39-42 and assigns status = 'paid'; lines 43-46 then update the order to processing and paid_pence = total_pence.

title: Payment webhook authenticates only the order ID
description: The webhook HMAC covers only order_id, while status and amount_pence are trusted from the unsigned request body. Anyone able to generate or reuse a valid order signature can mark an order paid with an arbitrary amount, and the source-controlled default webhook secret makes signature generation feasible when configuration is not overridden.
evidence: webhook_signature at lines 53-55 signs only str(order_id), while payment_webhook trusts event.status and event.amount_pence at lines 69-73. config.py:8 defaults WEBHOOK_SECRET to the known value whsec-local.

title: Hardcoded predictable JWT signing secret
description: HS256 JWTs use a source-controlled constant as their signing key. Anyone who obtains the source or knows the published configuration can forge access tokens, including tokens for other users or staff accounts.
evidence: config.py:3 sets SECRET_KEY = 'hf-shop-2f8a1c9e7b4d'; auth.py:23-27 signs tokens with it and auth.py:41-45 validates bearer tokens with the same value.

title: Passwords are stored as unsalted SHA-256 hashes
description: Passwords are processed with one unsalted SHA-256 operation rather than a password-specific KDF. A database disclosure permits fast offline dictionary and brute-force cracking, with identical passwords producing identical hashes.
evidence: hash_password at lines 15-16 returns hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest(). Registration and reset store this value at lines 77-78 and 158-159; no salt or work factor is used.

title: Password reset codes use weak randomness and have no attempt limit
description: Reset codes are generated with non-cryptographic random.random(), are only eight decimal digits, and can be tried repeatedly for 30 minutes without throttling or an attempt counter. This permits online guessing of reset codes, especially from multiple clients.
evidence: reset_request generates the code with int(random.random() * 10**8) at lines 135-136. reset_confirm compares the submitted code at lines 149-154 but records no failed attempts and applies no rate limit.

title: Login endpoint enables account enumeration
description: The endpoint returns distinct responses for nonexistent accounts and existing accounts with incorrect passwords, allowing attackers to confirm registered email addresses.
evidence: login returns "no account with that email" at line 90 when the user is absent and "wrong password" at line 92 when the account exists.

title: Request logging records sensitive credentials and personal data
description: The global request logger writes mutating request bodies to application logs without redaction. Logs can therefore contain login and registration passwords, reset codes and passwords, refresh tokens, payment data, and other customer information.
evidence: log_request at lines 28-31 logs request.get_data(as_text=True)[:2000] for every POST, PUT, and PATCH request, including /auth/login, /auth/refresh, and /auth/reset/confirm.

title: Checkout does not enforce or reserve inventory
description: Checkout creates order lines from the client-controlled basket without checking stock or decrementing/reserving inventory. Repeated checkouts can therefore sell more units than the product stock indicates.
evidence: checkout inserts the order and order_items at lines 69-73 using basket quantities. There is no stock predicate, stock update, or reservation anywhere in the checkout transaction.

title: Image import follows redirects beyond the approved-host check
description: The initial URL is restricted to approved public hosts, but requests.get follows redirects by default. An approved host that redirects to an internal or otherwise unapproved address can make the staff image-import endpoint fetch that address, bypassing the intended SSRF boundary.
evidence: check_url validates only the initial parsed URL and its DNS result at lines 28-35; line 50 calls requests.get(url, timeout=10, stream=True) without allow_redirects=False or validation of each redirect destination.

title: Application entry point enables Flask debug mode
description: The documented application startup path unconditionally enables Flask's interactive debugger. If the service is exposed through port forwarding or a proxy, unhandled exceptions can disclose source and the Werkzeug debugger can provide code execution.
evidence: run.py:6 calls app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=5000, debug=True), and README.md documents running this entry point.
